- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ -0.67), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential mean reversion or sentiment reversal.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days), leading to over-forecasted peaks; apply lagged smoothing or dampen momentum-driven forecasts.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use recent 7–14 day average as baseline for correction.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher prices when sentiment is positive; apply downward adjustment of 1–3% for 30d forecasts if sentiment > 0.67.
- If true outcome shows sharp downward correction after a spike, model often fails to anticipate; add a 2–5 day lagged correction rule for post-spike dips.
- Sentiment history with alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → -0.67 → 0.67) triggers model overfitting; apply smoothing filter or reduce volatility weight in forecast.
